title: 'Tis Midnight and on Olive's Brow
description: 'Tis Midnight and on Olive's Brow in Tonic Solfa: the solfa line by line with the words, staff notation, all 3 verses, and a piano to sing along with.
about: The words are by William Bingham Tappan, first published in 1822. The tune, ST. CROSS, is by John Bacchus Dykes (1861). This version of the melody and the words comes from the Open Hymnal Project.
underlay: 'Tis mid-night, and on Ol-ive's brow The star is dimmed that late-ly shone; 'Tis mid-night, in the gar-den now The suff-'ring Sa-vior prays a-lone.

lines: The star is dimmed that lately shone;
E'en the disciple whom He loved
Heeds not his Master's grief and tears.
Are borne the songs that angels know;
Unheard by mortals are the strains
That sweetly soothe the Savior's woe.
